memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And Noah did all that the Lord commanded him. Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came on the earth. And Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood. - Gen 7:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again we read those quietly powerful words: "Noah did all that the Lord commanded him." And now that obedience takes its most decisive step - Noah and his family actually enter the ark. All the years of building came down to this: walking through the door and trusting God to carry them through the storm.

Building the ark was faith at work over many years. But entering it was faith staking everything on God's word. Noah could have built the whole thing and still stayed outside, watching. Instead, he stepped in. There is a difference between admiring God's provision and actually entrusting yourself to it.

Many people today believe things about Jesus - that He is the Saviour, that His cross is the way to God. But believing about the ark would not have saved Noah. He had to get in. Saving faith is not just agreeing that Jesus can save; it is entrusting yourself entirely to Him, stepping inside, resting your whole weight on Him.

Noah at six hundred years old shows us it is never too late to obey God fully. Whatever your age or season, the call is the same - do all the Lord commands, and entrust yourself completely to the Saviour He has provided. Don't just admire the ark. Enter it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you merely admired Christ, or entrusted yourself fully to Him?
- Is there a step of obedient faith you know you need to take?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I don't want to just believe things about You - I want to entrust myself completely to You. Like Noah, help me step in, resting my whole weight on Christ my Saviour.
